claim: A task is the user's best guess at how to get an outcome; the lens asks what should happen next, the goal beyond the goal.
quote: When you give the model a task, it's executing your best guess at how to get the outcome you want.

refs.anchor: A task is the user's best guess at how to get an outcome

claim: Climb in rungs: each rewrite asks for the next outcome up, from the data to the decisions to the process, and the user climbs again from the result.
quote: Work out which three decisions are most urgent in the face of everything you've learned

claim: The top rung names the purpose, asks for a better way, shows from the organisation's own history that it would have caught things sooner, and runs it beside the current way for a cycle.
quote: show from our own history that it would have caught things sooner, and run it beside the current one for a quarter

refs.anchor: Where history exists, the prompt asks to show the new way would have worked on it

reason: the history check was there; the side-by-side run for one cycle was not

claim: Altitude fits tasks with an ultimate outcome and fits creative work less; a meeting about the work is the sign to use it.
quote: A good tell-tale sign that ambition in altitude is a good idea is if you're going to have meetings to discuss whatever you're working on.

refs.anchor: If the task has no outcome beyond itself
`/higher` if a meeting will discuss this

claim: Altitude is where durable workflows take the human out of the loop, and that needs the workflow changed: the model must be able to fetch the data, map versions to commits, and reach machines to reproduce and verify.
quote: in order to let Claude make sure our app is crash-free, I first had to make sure it can easily fetch crash reports, understand which app version maps to what git commit, and give it access to Windows, macOS, and Linux computers

claim: There are limits; the model handles higher abstraction as it grows, so climb one rung per call rather than asking for the top at once.
quote: "Claude, go make money" doesn't seem to work for most businesses by itself in 2026

claim: Depth means the tools, techniques, media and knowledge of the best professionals in the field, pushed until even they would learn something new.
quote: pushing the model to use the tools, techniques, media, and knowledge employed by the best professionals in the field

claim: Insist on the same instruments as the best in the field, because models switch vocabulary without switching methods; databases and statistical models over markdown tables.
quote: models often switch vocabulary without actually switching methods
reason: covered in behaviour: both deeper rewrites in the v0.4.0 run named runnable instruments (quantileExact, bootstrap interval, gh run view, stress-ng)

claim: Set an unreasonable target and state that it is reasonable; when a step looks impossible, say it is solvable and to keep going.
quote: Pick unreasonable goals and tell the model that they're very reasonable
reason: both deeper rewrites in the v0.4.0 behavioural run already set numeric targets (0 failures in 200 runs; within 5 percent of the dashboard) with no line asking for them, and no session showed a timid target; revisit if one does

claim: Challenge what you know: give the model the raw data and ask it to check the stated belief adversarially.
quote: Give the model access to the raw information and data and ask it to adversarially check assumptions.

claim: Produce new knowledge: once inside the data, ask for the blind spot nobody asked about, and show it holds on data it has not seen.
quote: find the earliest signal of churn we don't know about yet, and show it predicts on data it has not seen
reason: held-out data was there; the finding nobody asked about was not, and the flaky-test rewrite had no such ask

claim: Use an outside judge, never the model itself; best is a tool the model can run for immediate feedback.
quote: Do not ask the model to judge itself.

claim: The depth prompt asks four things before the rewrite: what a top professional would do that is not asked, the rawest material, the specific methods and tools, and what other than the model or the user shows the result is right.
quote: I want a deeper version of this task, not a bigger one.

refs.anchor: Make this task deeper, not bigger

claim: Range means more fields than were economical before, made practical by multi-agent systems.
quote: being ambitious in range means that we consider our work from the perspective of different fields - more fields than would have been economical in the past

refs.anchor: Wider means the task gets the methods of fields it would not normally afford
so each can run as its own subagent

claim: Replace the nouns with verbs: the review is not a deck, it is getting busy people to believe a story about cause and effect and to decide under uncertainty in 30 minutes.

Assemble a crew of fields chosen for the stakes and for the medium the result is delivered in, such as a motion and audio designer when it is presented, and include a red team that attacks the result.
quote: For production quality, I'd bring in an analyst, a journalist, and an editor.
reason: the crew ignored the medium: the review-deck rewrite for a Thursday meeting had no field that works in the room

claim: Avoid role play: use the fields to find methods, and ask for what a short seller does, not for writing like one.
quote: Don't ask the model to write like a short seller, ask it to do what a short seller does to research their position.

claim: Every kind of ambition needs the model to have a computer where it can install software and reach the relevant data.
quote: All the ways in which I describe ambition require the model to have a computer with the ability to install software and access to all kinds of relevant data
reason: the lenses can name the access; providing it is the user's setup

claim: Specific hard goals outperform telling people to try their best.
quote: humans who are given specific hard goals perform better than those who are simply told to try their best
reason: both deeper rewrites in the v0.4.0 behavioural run already set numeric targets (0 failures in 200 runs; within 5 percent of the dashboard) with no line asking for them, and no session showed a timid target; revisit if one does
